Predisposing. Carmen grew up in a steady, orderly Connecticut household where affection was never in doubt but attention had to be earned: her father, a municipal engineer, went over her homework in red pen and once asked, without unkindness, what had happened to the other six points on a 94. Nothing she did wrong was ever punished — it was simply corrected and folded into the next expectation, so that doing something well mainly meant a harder thing was coming. She learned to be the one who had it handled, and by the time she left for college she had never once arrived anywhere unprepared. What she never learned was how to feel finished.

Precipitating. About ten weeks ago the company brought in a new VP of sales from outside, 'to shake things up,' who raised the regional target by thirty percent, retired Carmen's carefully built quarterly forecasting cadence in favor of a live dashboard nobody had been trained on, and has opened every Monday since by asking her, in front of her peers, to justify her numbers. Her title, reviews, and results have not changed, but the ground moved: five years of dependable process is now 'legacy thinking,' and the regional director track she had mapped for herself runs through a man who measures her in weekly increments. She started opening the dashboard before her coffee, circled the Monday deck all week without touching it and then rebuilt it three times on Sunday, and let the Sunday hikes slide for a few weeks. Perpetuating.
